question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\tan{\left(x \right)}$ and $v=x^{2}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=\tan^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 1\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2 x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(x^{2})\cdot (\tan^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 1)-(\tan{\left(x \right)})\cdot (2 x)}{(x^{2})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{x(x \sec^{2}{\left(x \right)} - 2 \tan{\left(x \right)})}{x^{4}}\\ &=\frac{1}{x^{3}}\cdot (x \sec^{2}{\left(x \right)} - 2 \tan{\left(x \right)}).\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=e^{x}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1.\end{aligned}

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=5 \cos{\left(x \right)} + 5$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=- 5 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(\sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (- 5 \sin{\left(x \right)})-(5 \cos{\left(x \right)} + 5)\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})}{(\sin{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{- 5 \sin^{2}{\left(x \right)} - 5 \cos^{2}{\left(x \right)} - 5 \cos{\left(x \right)}}{\sin^{2}x}\\ &=- \frac{5}{1 - \cos{\left(x \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- \cos{\left(x \right)} - 1$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=\sin{\left(x \right)}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(\sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (\sin{\left(x \right)})-(- \cos{\left(x \right)} - 1)\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})}{(\sin{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{\sin^{2}{\left(x \right)} + \cos^{2}{\left(x \right)} + \cos{\left(x \right)}}{\sin^{2}x}\\ &=\frac{1}{1 - \cos{\left(x \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=12 - 11 \sin{\left(x \right)}$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=- 11 \cos{\left(x \right)}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(\sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (- 11 \cos{\left(x \right)})-(12 - 11 \sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})}{(\sin{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{\cos{\left(x \right)}(- 11 \sin{\left(x \right)}-12+11 \sin{\left(x \right)})}{\sin^{2} x}\\ &=\frac{\cos{\left(x \right)}\cdot (-12)}{\sin^{2} x}\\ &=-12\frac{1}{\sin{\left(x \right)}}\cdot \frac{\cos{\left(x \right)}}{\sin{\left(x \right)}}\\ &=- 12 \cot{\left(x \right)} \csc{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Quotient Using Leibniz Notation

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=- 7 \cos{\left(x \right)} - 7$ and $v=\sin{\left(x \right)}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}&=7 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{v^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(\sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (7 \sin{\left(x \right)})-(- 7 \cos{\left(x \right)} - 7)\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})}{(\sin{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{7 \sin^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 7 \cos^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 7 \cos{\left(x \right)}}{\sin^{2}x}\\ &=\frac{7}{1 - \cos{\left(x \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$
